questions.prompt: Which statement best describes constitutional change in practice?
choices: Only formal amendments can change constitutional meaning.
Only the Supreme Court can shape constitutional meaning.
Text, amendment, statute, precedent, executive practice, federalism, and political development can all shape constitutional practice.
Public opinion automatically changes constitutional text.
questions.explanation: Constitutional development occurs through multiple institutional and legal pathways.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 34

The legal rule and result necessary to decide the case before the court
questions.explanation: The holding is the legal determination necessary to resolve the case, not every statement in the opinion.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 34

questions.prompt: Why can a Supreme Court decision require further institutional action?
choices: The Court writes every implementing regulation itself.
Judicial decisions may require lower courts, agencies, legislatures, executives, or other institutions to implement remedies or change practice.
Supreme Court decisions are merely advisory.
Implementation is unrelated to constitutional law.
questions.explanation: Courts decide cases and remedies, but implementation often depends on other institutions.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 34

questions.prompt: Which factor is most relevant to a principled stare decisis analysis?
choices: Whether the current outcome is popular
Whether the precedent is workable, legally justified, doctrinally consistent, and relied upon
Whether social media supports the ruling
questions.explanation: Precedent analysis considers legal error, workability, reliance, consistency, factual change, and related jurisprudential factors.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 34

questions.prompt: What is one central tradeoff of federalism?
choices: It guarantees identical policy in every state.
It can enable local experimentation while also producing unequal rights, services, or administrative capacity.
It prevents courts from reviewing state action.
questions.explanation: Federalism can support variation and experimentation while creating uneven outcomes across jurisdictions.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 34
